purpose: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including ear infections, throat infections, skin infections, and certain chest infections like pneumonia. It can also be used in people who are allergic to penicillin as an alternative antibiotic. Your doctor may also prescribe it to prevent certain infections from coming back.
how_it_works: This medicine works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Without those proteins, the bacteria cannot survive and spread. This gives your immune system a chance to clear the infection from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related, including nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and diarrhea. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset. Some people may also notice a mild skin rash or feel generally unwell.
warnings: Let your doctor know if you have liver problems, as this medication can sometimes affect the liver. Tell your healthcare provider about all other medications you take, because erythromycin can interact with many common drugs and cause serious reactions. Stop taking it and seek medical help right away if you develop a severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, irregular heartbeat, or severe diarrhea, as these can be signs of a serious reaction.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 400 mg taken by mouth every 6 hours, or 800 mg every 12 hours, depending on the type of infection. For children, the dose is based on their weight. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
